metadata.title: Tech Stocks Stall Into Thanksgiving: Will the AI Rebound Return?

content.text:
Tech stocks stalled Wednesday as the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.6% and Nvidia (NVDA) lost 4%. AI spending doubts and fresh inflation data cut short Monday's rebound.
Still, the Nasdaq recovered from steeper intraday losses, even as chip stocks closed lower. That leaves holders of Nvidia, Micron Technology (MU), and Oracle (ORCL) exposed when markets reopen Friday for a shortened session.
Why Did the Tech Stocks Rebound Fade So Fast?
Nvidia posted one of its best sessions on record Monday. Jensen Huang had just returned as CEO after resigning on Nov. 12.
However, Nvidia has since slid, including 4% Wednesday, while Micron lost 4% and Oracle fell over 5%.
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Marvell Technology (MRVL), and Intel (INTC) edged lower. Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor exchange-traded fund (ETF), ticker SMH, shed 1%.
The weakness had already spread to Asia. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell more than 7% in an Asian chip sell-off earlier Wednesday.
Is This Panic or a Macro Warning?
Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation, which excludes food and energy, rose 3.3% from a year earlier in October.
Economists had forecast 3.2%, according to Morningstar. As a result, worries grew that higher interest rates would weigh on growth stocks.
Venu Krishna, head of U.S. equity strategy at Barclays, offered a blunt read on CNBC.
"We just feel that this is panic right now."
Krishna added.
"What the market is telling you is that the AI growth narrative has hit a wall and given the centrality of that theme at the economic level, the market is expecting some sort of a macro shock."
In contrast, Anthropic (ANT), the maker of the Claude AI model, bucked the trend. Its shares gained more than 4% after slipping below the $83 initial public offering (IPO) price.
Elsewhere, Michael Burry disclosed a temporary bullish shift Wednesday after the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20% below its record.
Markets reopen Friday for a shortened session. The AI trade may hinge on whether rate fears ease and whether AI spending begins to pay off.
Read the Original story Tech Stocks Stall Into Thanksgiving: Will the AI Rebound Return? by Darryn Pollock at beincrypto.com
